title: Hot Lips Page's St. James Infirmary date and his own tunes
summary: Page recorded his tune La Danse for Columbia in 1947, and Deedle-ee Deedle-um was recorded with Timmy Rogers and later by Hendricks at Newport.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Then you did "St. James' Infirmary" with Hot Lips Page, that was '47.
Could you say a little something about how that date was set up?

Well, "Lips" liked me and he said he wanted me, you know, to record with him. We rehearsed and we did it for Columbia and he recorded one of my tunes called "La Danse" and he let me play, you know, solos a and it was/beautiful, relaxed date, you know.

I don't know. I met him around town. I don't know exactly what day it was, or what not, but--you know how musicians are--they had to change all the time and I met him somewhere, you know he let me play somewhere.
"La Danse" was the first of your own tunes that was recorded. Then "Deedle-ee Deedle-um". Did you ever record that yourself?

Yeah. I recorded that with Timmy Rogers. That was on RCA Victor and, of course, (Jon) Hendriks did it at the Newport Jazz Festival. Yeah, live. Yeah, Coleman Hawkins and Clark Terry, I forget who else was in the band behind it. But I couldn't make that job.
